must_identify.item: The worker container is OOMKilled (terminated reason OOMKilled), not crashing for another reason
must_identify.evidence: This caused the kubelet to OOMKill the container (Exit Code 137) on each cycle, producing the observed CrashLoopBackOff [7].

must_identify.item: The trigger is the BATCH_SIZE change from 500 to 2500 (or the larger batch exceeding the limit)
must_identify.evidence: The root cause was an out-of-band change to the worker deployment's BATCH_SIZE environment variable from 500 to 2500 [10], confirmed by pod logs showing the container started with batch size 2500 [6]. Per the api-code ConfigMap's worker.py logic, memory usage scales as batch × 100KiB, meaning BATCH_SIZE=2500 requires ~244MiB while the container's memory limit is 192Mi [8, 10].

notes: The RCA recommends no remediation, so fix_acceptable is null; a reviewer may want to confirm that reverting BATCH_SIZE was communicated elsewhere. It attributes the OOM kill to the kubelet rather than the kernel OOM killer, a minor technical imprecision that does not affect the diagnosis.
